title: History of Neurofeedback
subtitle: From conditioning animal rhythms to modern closed-loop training
altText: Chalkboard-style clinical diagram illustrating history of neurofeedback within a neurofeedback closed loop.
learningObjectives: Explain history of neurofeedback without diagnostic overreach.
Distinguish measurement, mechanism and clinical outcome in history of neurofeedback.
Identify one safety or validity limitation relevant to history of neurofeedback.

sections.explainSimply: Neurofeedback developed from biofeedback and operant-conditioning research in which measurable physiological activity was returned to a learner as feedback.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: Historically important findings established that some brain signals can be shaped through contingent feedback, but early clinical enthusiasm often outpaced controlled evidence.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: Modern neurofeedback includes EEG, slow cortical potential, source-based, haemodynamic and imaging-based approaches. Historical claims should be separated from contemporary evidence standards.
sections.thinkOfItLike: A driving instructor who gives immediate dashboard feedback while the learner practises a controllable skill.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Psychologists need to understand history of neurofeedback to evaluate mechanism claims, informed consent, treatment fit and whether change transfers to real-world function.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: Do not treat longevity of use as proof of efficacy.
sections.clinicalPearl: The trained metric is an intermediate target; the clinical endpoint is meaningful function.
sections.practicalExample: A clinician using history of neurofeedback predefines the target, checks raw signal and artifacts, monitors symptoms and function, and reviews whether change generalises beyond the feedback display.
sections.limitationsCautions: Do not treat longevity of use as proof of efficacy. Evidence classification: established mechanism; mixed clinical evidence.
